_comment: Which targets a round 10 measures. Everything registered in
harness/targets_r10.py runs unless it is switched off here, and this file
ships with nothing switched off.
disabled  run everything except these
only      run exactly these and ignore the rest
`only` wins over `disabled` when both are set. Command line flags win over
both: --only and --disable on run_r10.py override whatever is here, so a
one-off narrow pass never needs this file edited.
A name that is not registered is a hard error rather than a silent skip.
A round that quietly measured nine targets because one was misspelled
would publish a field that never existed.
Registered names: raw, zurg, altmount, infinidysk, nzbdav-og, nzbdavex,
decypharr, stremthru, aiostreams, streamnzb, comet.
raw is the transport ceiling rather than a competitor. Disabling it is
allowed and costs the run its denominator: every MB/s becomes a number
with nothing to read it against, which is the state rounds 3 to 9 were in.
comet is the one target expected to cost more than it returns. It has no
import API and deadlocks its own SQLite under sustained load at its
shipped defaults. It is on by default like everything else and it has a
shorter budget, so it abandons its own rows instead of the round. Add it
to `disabled` to stop paying for that.
